//: THE SHARED MACHINE-TRANSPORT CONTRACT. Read tests/machine-transport/README.md before editing.
//contract: Each scenario is an argv a client wants to run on a MACHINE over SSH.
SSH has no argv API: a command is sent as ONE string the remote shell re-parses.
So every transport must compose that string identically, and every transport
must end up delivering the SAME argv to the remote process.
Three legs consume this file, and all three must agree:
3. Dart  (shed-mobile, via the FRB bridge)            -> both goldens
Adding a scenario means re-recording BOTH goldens (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1) and
re-running the Dart leg in shed-mobile. A scenario is never removed to make
//version: The contract revision. Bump on any change to `scenarios`; the Dart leg pins it so a silent divergence between the two repos is impossible.

scenarios.why: the ordinary case: bare-safe tokens only
rc_bin is routinely an absolute path — ~/.local/bin is not on the non-login SSH PATH
the shape every real create takes
a display name with a space — the most common non-trivial case
an empty argv element must survive as an explicit empty argument, not vanish
the quoter's own escape character; the classic off-by-one in hand-rolled quoting
must not be treated as a quoting character by either side
backslash is literal inside single quotes; a double-quoting transport would mangle it
must NOT be expanded by the remote shell — the whole point of quoting
an injection attempt via backticks and $() must reach the process as literal text
the injection case the always-quoter exists to close
a newline inside a quoted argument must survive as one argument, not split into two
internal whitespace must not re-split the argument
a value that looks like a flag must stay a value
non-ASCII must round-trip byte-for-byte through both transports
tilde expansion must NOT happen — a literal ~ is a legitimate name
a full realistic create, end to end
